video.title: Biggest Fantasy Basketball Risers & Fallers | Usage & Minutes Changes for 2026

summary: Josh Lloyd goes through his projected biggest minutes and usage risers and fallers for the 2026 season. He says usage and minutes have the strongest link to fantasy value. Minutes risers: Coby White, Jalen Green, Khaman Maluach, Joan Beringer and Jonathan Kuminga, who signed with Minnesota and is expected to start. Usage risers: Brandon Ingram (assumed to be moving to the Clippers), Collin Murray-Boyles, Kon Knueppel, Julius Randle and Matas Buzelis, whom he calls a top 50 player. Minutes fallers: Nikola Vucevic, Kevin Porter Jr., Bennedict Mathurin (just signed by the Pelicans), Santi Aldama and Kyle Filipowski. Usage fallers: Michael Porter Jr., Jaylen Brown, Alex Sarr, Jrue Holiday and Ja Morant, with Tyrese Maxey also likely losing usage.

rules.text: Usage and minutes are the two stats most closely tied to fantasy value. Projecting changes in them gives a starting point for valuing players.
rules.quote: usage and minutes are the two biggest correlations of stats for fantasy value

rules.text: Look at context behind last season's numbers, such as injuries, minutes limits or a tanking team, before projecting a player forward.
rules.quote: But context around it is important. So, Jaylen Green played 25.9 minutes per game last season.

rules.text: For uncertain young players with upside, take a flier with your last pick and cut him if it does not work out.
rules.quote: you just take a fly with the last pick and just see what happens. And then you cut him.

rules.text: A backup big's upside often depends on an injury to the starter, so he is mainly worth it if you have room to stash him.
rules.quote: But the upside only is there if you've got stash ability waiting for a go bear injury

rules.text: In points leagues, a scorer who does little else needs both minutes and shot volume to succeed.
rules.quote: And to be successful there, you need the minutes, which he's going to get, but then you also need volume.

rules.text: He advises against being okay with injury risk when drafting injury-prone players.
rules.quote: player if you're okay with injury risk, which I don't think you should be

rules.text: A recurring back injury during a season can improve with a full offseason of rest. Worry again only if it flares up in training camp.
rules.quote: But you have four months off and then theoretically like hopefully your back is okay.

rules.text: When high-usage players join the same team, last season's numbers cannot all hold. Expect each player's usage to drop.
rules.quote: If you just put everyone's numbers from the year before, the last time they played together, they're going

rules.text: A player losing about 25% of his usage cannot keep his fantasy output, even if his minutes stay high.
rules.quote: if you are losing a chunk like that 25% of your usage not 25 percentage points

rules.text: General rules like third-year breakouts are a good baseline, but each player should then be judged on his own situation.
rules.quote: you look at things generally to start off to set a baseline what's the expectation
